analysis.one_line_summary: Creator demonstrates step-by-step how to get a bouncy blowout on short layered hair using the Wavytalk thermal heated brush.
analysis.full_description: A creator shows her styling routine for short layered dark hair. The video opens with a completed bouncy blowout result hook, then cuts to rough drying her hair with a hair dryer, before showing the Wavytalk heated round brush. She demonstrates curling the ends outward in three sections, curling face-framing layers inward, smoothing the top section, and rolling back her curtain bangs for a swoop effect. The video finishes with her admiring the bouncy, voluminous results and blowing a kiss to the camera.

analysis.transcript_full_original: This is how I get that bouncy blowout look on my short hair. I recently added layers and I feel like this is the best way for me to style it. I use the Wavytalk heated brush. I only really separate my hair into like three sections because I'm lazy, but I basically just flip the ends outwards, adding a lot of tension, and I just find that this method for me is much easier than using a blow dry brush. I also make sure to flip the front pieces of my hair inwards instead of outwards, just so that those pieces can frame my face. And now I go ahead and do the top layer. This for me is the most important part and the part where I focus the most on and take the most time, just because I want it to be nice and sleek. For the bangs, I roll away from my face while pulling the brush towards my face, if that makes sense. And that's just been the easiest way for me to get that swoop of the curtain bang. And then I just do one more touch up of the front pieces, and that's pretty much how I style my hair every single time. It gives me that nice bouncy blowout look, and I love it.
